title: Stream congestion & L2 misalignment - Nsight snapshots
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of an odd perf pattern seen in the 4xA100 staging cluster: end-to-end latency regresses intermittently on medium-length requests (16-64 tokens) despite stable GPU SM utilization and token throughput. Hypothesis: stream-level congestion interacting with L2 cache line alignment is causing kernel tail latency spikes and underutilized warps in critical attention kernels.

Background / context:
- Workload: decoder-only transformer (gpt-like) with kv-cache, batch sizes usually 1-8, dynamic sequence lengths 16-128.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 40GB (108 SMs) in 4x config, CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.0; Nsight Systems 2024.5 captures.
- Runtime: Redwood serving-runtime branch: feature/kv-prefetch (PR 482). We recently enabled concurrent host->device async copies on stream 3 and kernel launches on stream 0 as part of prefetch window experiment.

What I ran (recipe):
- Baseline: single-stream capture (all memcpy+kernels on default stream) with sequence lengths 64 and batch=4.
- Parallel experiment: host->device prefetch on stream 3 (cudaMemcpyAsync with priority low), kernels launched on stream 0.
- Compare: 100 repeated inference requests (warm cache) captured with Nsight, sampling range focusing on tail latencies.
- Nsight settings: timeline + CUDA API tracing + unified memory metrics + L2 hit/miss counters.

Key Nsight observations (summary):
1) Apparent contradiction: SM active and theoretical occupancy metrics show ~0.55 occupancy and 85-90% SM utilization for attention_forward kernel. However P50 latency stable but P95 spikes correlate with additional small memcpy bursts on stream 3.
2) Kernel timeline shows many small kernel launches (attention tiles) separated by short gaps (~200-400us). When a memcpy burst occurs it appears to evict useful L2 lines and next kernel experiences ~30-40% increase in DRAM read latency (per L2 miss counter), causing longer kernel tail.
3) Warp efficiency for the attention kernel drops from 92% -> 68% in spike events. Active warps per SM stays similar but divergence increases (indication of thread divergence or cache/TLB stalls).
4) CUDA graph captures (we tried capturing a 64-token step) reduce API overhead but do not eliminate the tail: when graphs include prefetch memcpy nodes, graph execution triggers the same L2 churn pattern.

Micro-data points from a representative spike window:
- attention_forward (tile 0): occupancy 0.53, active_warps/SM avg 22, avg_warp_efficiency 0.91, but during spike tail: warp_efficiency 0.67, l2_miss_rate +37%, average DRAM latency +120ns.
- kv_write kernel: short but synchronous memcpy afterwards appears to overlap with other streams; memory copy size ~1.2MB aligns to 128B lines but starting addresses vary by shard, causing line misalignment.

Initial hypothesis (refined):
- Concurrent memcpy on an auxiliary stream causes L2 evictions that are not bulk-friendly (small, misaligned copies), creating churn in L2 and increasing misses for the subsequent attention tiles which are latency-sensitive to per-warp cache locality. Because attention kernels are tiled, they touch the same cache lines across tiles; misaligned small memcopies break spatial locality and increase conflict misses.
- Additionally, stream scheduling at the driver level can reorder small kernels and copies; small gaps between tile kernels means the L2 doesn't have time to warm back up, amplifying the tail.

Evidence for misalignment:
- cuobjdump /device pointers show that prefetch buffers are allocated with malloc-aligned offsets but the copy offsets used by the prefetch scheduler have a variable offset due to rounding in our allocator. Some copies start at address +0x30 (48B) rather than 128B, meaning copies span cache lines unpredictably.
- Traces where we force the prefetch to use 128B-aligned addresses show reduced L2 miss spikes and fewer tail outliers.

Experiments performed & results (short):
1) Force 128B-aligned allocations for prefetch buffers -> P95 latency drops ~18%, P99 drops ~25% for seq64 workload.
2) Serialize memcpys (do not run prefetch concurrently) -> tail spikes disappear, but end-to-end throughput drops 6-8% (expected).
3) Increase prefetch chunk size to 4MB -> fewer, larger copies reduce L2 churn but increase peak memory pressure; P95 improved for busy runs but worst-case OOM risk increased.
4) Run with CUDA graphs that exclude prefetch memcpys (i.e., prefetch done on host before graph launch) -> tail reduced, but API complexity increased.

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Is L2 miss rate the primary contributor or are we also seeing TLB shootdowns / page table contention due to many small pinned allocations? Nsight didn't directly show TLB events; need lower-level metrics (SASS/perf counters) or ptxas insights.
- Driver scheduling: are small kernel gaps being preempted by lower priority DMA that reorder execution? Need to correlate with driver GPU timeline priority lanes.
- Does this pattern generalize to other Ampere/Blackwell cards? We have limited tests on V100 and RTX6000 — schedule similar but magnitude differs.

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Short-term mitigation: change prefetch allocator to 128B-aligned and increase minimum chunk size to 256KB to reduce number of small memcpys. Roll as feature flag in staging (INF-3245).
- Measurement: add nsight session annotated with cudaMemPrefetchAsync offsets + show L2 miss counters per kernel in our tracing pipeline. Attach session ID NSIGHT_SESSION:nsight://2025-09-14-stream-l2-01.
- Deeper profiling: produce SASS-level counters using cupti/KPIs for TLB, L2 sector misses. Consider running nvprof/cupti microbench for a single SM pinned run to isolate.
- Long-term: consider (a) coalescing prefetches into fewer larger DMA ops, (b) using prefetch hinting to avoid L2 (if possible), or (c) move prefetch to a different memory region cached differently (e.g., use device-local slabs aligned to cache lines).

Action items assigned:
- Diego: implement 128B alignment + 256KB min chunk in prefetch allocator, add flag prefetch.align=true (deadline: 2025-09-26).
- Lena: run A/B Nsight captures on 2x different instance types (A100 and H100 if available) and collect SASS counters where possible (deadline: 2025-09-28).
- Kai: draft a short tech note for product on tradeoffs (latency vs throughput vs memory). Include example of host->device serialization costs. (draft due 2025-10-02).

Notes to self / stream-of-consciousness:
- Weird that occupancy numbers look healthy while warp efficiency drops. Reminds me of earlier microbatch fragmentation bug — basically occupancy is a coarse-grained metric; tile-local cache effects dominate tail.
- Should test with stress background memcpy noise on a separate GPU to emulate noisy neighbor and see if same pattern repeats (helps reason about dedicated vs noisy environments).
- If alignment change fixes >80% of spikes we can consider enabling by default in Dedicated pools where memory safety and throughput matters.

References / traces:
- Nsight session: nsight://2025-09-14-stream-l2-01 (attached to linked_artifacts above).
- Jira INF-3245: feature/kv-prefetch followups.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482 (prefetch allocator prototype).

End of notes.

-- Asha
